title: syncr / Plan pipeline
description: Solve outcomes and durations, the supersession ratio, queue delay, empty slots by reason, and projection outcomes. Every family here is recorded in the WORKER process, which is why the scrape configuration has a job of its own for it: scraping only the api would leave this entire dashboard empty.

panels.title: Solve outcomes
panels.description: Solves per hour by how they ended. A SUPERSEDED SOLVE IS NORMAL: it is the expected outcome of editing quickly, which is why no alert fires on the event and only a sustained ratio is a signal.

panels.title: Solve duration, p50 and p99
panels.description: Section 19 budgets a full one-week solve at under 2 seconds. It runs in the worker, so the budget is generous.

panels.title: Supersession ratio, over one hour
panels.description: The health signal for the debounce value. The design guarantees at most one discarded solve per burst, so a SUSTAINED ratio above roughly 0.3 means the debounce window is too short for how this user actually edits, and the value should be revisited rather than tolerated. This is the same query SupersededRatioHigh and docs/runbooks/debounce-tuning.md are stated over.

panels.title: Operation queue delay, p99 by kind
panels.description: How long a claim waited past the instant it was due. Observed at the CLAIM rather than at the finish, so it measures the worker falling behind rather than the work's own duration. A debounced solve is due 1500 ms after the mutation; a delay far above the tick interval means the tick is spending its time elsewhere.

panels.title: Empty slots by reason
panels.description: Discretionary time no block was placed in, and why. A slot the solver could not fill for a stated reason is the plan explaining itself; a rising count under one reason is where to look next.

panels.title: Projection outcomes, and whether writes are permitted
panels.description: A refused projection is recorded as FAILED deliberately, because the consequence is identical: the plan is not reaching the phone. The arming gauge is what separates 'syncr cannot write' from 'syncr is not permitted to write', and it is why ProjectionFailing can be stated without either always firing or never firing. Writes are off in every deployment until a person has run the live Google suite.

panels.title: Weeks inside the horizon with no plan
panels.description: Should sit at zero. A sustained non-zero value means the plan-horizon maintainer is not keeping up or is failing, which is the failure mode that would otherwise present to the user as a calendar that goes blank at a week boundary. The second series is the maintainer's contained faults, which never reach the gauge: a runner that raises every pass leaves the gauge at whatever it last set.

panels.title: Materializations by cause, and verdict transitions
panels.description: A materialization caused by solve_failed is a week that fell back to a derived-only plan: expected to be zero in normal operation, and a non-zero value is a solver problem surfacing as a degraded plan rather than as an outage. The transition counter carries provenance, direction and surface, so a capacity warning is distinguishable from an authoritative finding.

panels.title: Operations stuck, races lost, and contained solve faults
panels.description: Three families with no alert of their own, drawn together because each is a contained fault: a non-terminal operation count that will not fall, a claim or reaper race the loser recorded, and a solve pass that raised outside the outcomes the coordinator records. SolveFailing reads the last of these directly, because a pass that raises never reaches the line that records a failed outcome.

panels.title: Solve shape: iterations and blocks placed
panels.description: What a solve actually did. Roughly 210 blocks at 30 per day is the reference week; a placement count that falls while iterations rise is the search working harder for less.
